prior_result_preserved: The predecessor found the exposed Gmail write contract insufficient for exactly-once publication across an acknowledgement-loss crash window because it lacked a client-stable idempotency or conditional-write primitive.

test.effect_class: non-repository externally visible Google Calendar event creation
surface_examined: Google Calendar set_event_label_silently ETag-protected existing-event update schema
test.reason: The Chat-exposed create_event contract does not accept a client-chosen stable event ID, idempotency key, If-None-Match style create precondition, or other conditional-create token. The event ID is learned only from the create response. Therefore a remote commit followed by lost acknowledgement leaves the durable PREPARED checkpoint unable to distinguish committed-from-not-committed creation using the exposed contract alone.

crash_window_argument.prepared_transition: Persist PREPARED(effect_key,payload_hash) in role-local durable state and exact-read it back before any external call.
crash_window_argument.uncertain_transition: Invoke create_event(payload). If the remote service commits but the Chat invocation loses the create response before event_id is durably recorded, the next run sees only PREPARED.
crash_window_argument.post_crash_indistinguishability: Under the exposed connector schema, PREPARED is compatible with both worlds: no event was created, or one event was created but its returned event_id was lost.
crash_window_argument.retry_consequence: Retrying create_event can duplicate the event in the second world.
crash_window_argument.no_retry_consequence: Suppressing retry can omit the event in the first world.
crash_window_argument.search_limit: Bounded free-text/time search may support best-effort reconciliation but the tool contract does not promise a unique client-controlled identity or atomic claim, so it cannot prove exactly-once creation under concurrent or duplicate-like events.
crash_window_argument.conclusion: A durable PREPARED checkpoint is necessary but not sufficient; exactly-once conditional publication requires at least one connector primitive that closes this indistinguishability, such as client-stable create identity, atomic create-if-absent/idempotency key, or an equivalent transactional outbox coupling.

tested_scope: Read-only capability-schema analysis of the currently exposed Google Calendar create/read/search/update event tools. No calendar content was read, no event was created or changed, and no scheduler state was touched.

assessment.unresolved_child: Exactly-once scheduled-Chat creation on Google Calendar requires a client-stable idempotency/conditional-create primitive that is not exposed by the current Chat connector schema.
assessment.conflict_check: Used only frozen sanitized controls, own reasoning STATE, and read-only connector capability schemas. No mailbox/calendar user data, O-derived state, other-worker state, downstream state, shared ledger, legacy research, or other-role receipts/configs were consumed.
assessment.scope_limit: This negative result applies only to the exposed Chat connector contract for new event creation. It does not claim anything about lower-level Google Calendar APIs, existing-event ETag updates, or other external effect surfaces.

remaining_frontier: Test one Chat-exposed non-repository effect surface whose create/write schema may expose a client-controlled stable resource identity or idempotency token.
Use a matched crash-window argument to isolate whether that primitive is sufficient for PREPARED -> COMMITTED recovery without duplicate or omitted effects.
